A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same NOVER study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen evaluations, reward-component ablations, reasoning analyses, and a human preference study using 100 examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The reasoning-perplexity proxy, policy-proxy synchronization, reward components, and GRPO procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. Section 6.6 explains the existing inverse incentive procedure differently without changing its operation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Natural Reasoning, General Thoughts, WebInstruct, SS-GEN, EmoBench, ToMBench, OPUS, and FANToM. The additional model experiments reuse existing reasoning datasets; preprocessing and dataset statistics move to Appendix A.

E2.justification: The Base, CoT, and SFT comparison procedures are reused for the additional backbones. The Qwen-Instruct/R1-Distill comparisons and WebInstruct GV, LJ, and LJS comparator sets remain unchanged. ReAct is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations using Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B instruct checkpoints, extending the original Qwen pretrained-checkpoint configurations. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and hyperparameters are retained; newly specified judge settings are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: v2 removes Section 6.3's explicit report of stable training beyond 200,000 steps without collapse or explosion. The component ablations, distribution and length analyses, reasoning-pattern analysis, false-premise examples, and human preference study remain.

E5.justification: v1 Section 5 states that all results are averaged over three runs; v2 removes this statement without providing replacement run-count information. This changes statistical reporting, without establishing that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 substantially extends the main results beyond Qwen to two additional model families. NOVER's NR/GT/WI scores are 40.70/41.50/34.00% for Llama and 32.20/21.90/29.30% for Mistral. Advantages are not universal: Llama SFT scores 34.50% on WI, and the Mistral baseline scores 33.00% on NR. Existing numerical results are unchanged; the extended-stability finding is removed.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix E's entire equivalence proof, including Equations 14–23, is removed. It established identical group-normalized advantages for absolute and relative perplexity. v2 retains the corresponding rationale in Section 4.3 but provides no replacement derivation; the main method equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: verifier-free incentive training from SFT data, broad text-to-text applicability, the reported 7.7% advantage, and inverse incentive training.

C2.justification: v2 explains why the additional model families require instruct checkpoints and adds a rubric-training limitation involving repetitive story text and absent process rewards. It removes the large-model scaling limitation and coordinated-scaling discussion. The older Qwen-only explanation remains in Limitations despite the added experiments.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E substantially expand prompt documentation, including strict and lenient judging templates and general-verifier decoding settings of temperature 0.0 and 1,024 maximum tokens. The GitHub code footnote is replaced by a Hugging Face Spaces link, while explicit story/assessment tag names are omitted. Existing split and hyperparameter details are relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds a ReAct discussion and citation, plus references for Llama 3 and Mistral. The broader positioning against verifier-dependent incentive training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial restructuring moves dataset construction, training settings, human-evaluation rubrics, and reasoning-pattern definitions from the main text into Appendices A, C, I, and J. Prompt appendices are added, while inverse-training explanations and reward-hacking prose are rewritten or condensed.

P2.justification: v2 adds a model-results table and six standalone prompt figures, partly redisplaying previously illustrated prompt content. Dataset and hyperparameter tables move to appendices, Figure 1 is redrawn and corrects RLFH to RLHF, and the FANToM example is compressed into one column. Existing experimental plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional model-family results and explicit judge prompts modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility; the new rubric-training caveat also improves qualification. These benefits are tempered by removal of the three-run disclosure and equivalence proof, and by the outdated Qwen-only limitations text. The net improvement is useful but limited.
